result.title: Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation for Wind Energy Predictive Analysis
result.comment: To be published in IEEE BigData 2026 Conference
result.summary: Resource-constrained cyber-physical decision systems often apply fixed sensing, knowledge, and computational pipelines despite state-dependent information needs. We introduce Minimum-Sufficient Knowledge and Computation (MSKC), a resource-aware computing principle: select the least-costly route meeting decision-risk and deployment constraints, escalating only when cheaper routes are insufficient. As proof of concept, we isolate adaptive knowledge routing, the decision underlying Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning (KGML), which conventionally injects external knowledge unconditionally rather than only where needed. We instantiate this for wind ramp-event predictive analysis, an edge-oriented decision-support task, evaluating local, relational, and physics-informed routes with a state-aware gate on publicly available real data from two wind farms. We establish conditions for feasibility preservation, cost dominance, and strict expected savings over always-on routing. At a 35.9% relational-knowledge injection rate, adaptive routing is statistically indistinguishable from always-on injection on the reported metrics while reducing knowledge calls by 64%, supporting sustainable, Green-IT-aligned deployment. These results support MSKC's premise that uniformly maximal intelligence is unnecessary. This offers intelligent data analysis for big data streams: the analysis itself decides, per state, how much knowledge and computation the data warrant.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「最小充分知识与计算」（MSKC）原则，在风电场功率爬坡事件预测中实例化自适应知识路由：以状态感知门控在本地、关系与物理先验三条路线间按需升级，并给出可行性保持、成本占优与期望节省的条件及真实数据验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按状态选择最低成本路径、不足才升级」的门控与成本占优分析，可能为 LVR 的动态计算分配与停止决策（THINK/LOOK/STOP 的收益成本权衡）提供问题表述参考，但无视觉或 latent 状态内容，跨域可迁移性有待核查。
